title: KV cache throughput/latency/memory harness and regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective:
Run a repeatable, automated load-testing and benchmarking harness focused on the KV/prefix cache layer to quantify trade-offs between hit rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and memory footprint. We want both steady-state and burst behaviors and a regression detection pipeline that alerts on regressions vs a golden baseline.

Background:
Previous perf work improved batching and KV eviction heuristics but we lack a systematic way to answer: for a given cache budget and workload mix (many short prefixes vs long-context reuse), how does hit rate map to observed p95 generation latency and end-to-end tokens/sec? Engineering teams have been running ad-hoc experiments; this ticket centralizes harness and CI gating.

Success criteria:
- Harness that can run on k8s CI cluster and produce a standardized artifact (JSON + flamegraphs + histogram PDF).
- Reproducible experiments for at least three workload profiles: high-reuse short-prefix, mixed, low-reuse long-prefix.
- Detect regressions: alert if p95 increases >12% or tokens/sec drops >10% vs baseline for identical config, or memory growth >15% for same hit rate.
- Provide a tuning guide (cache size, TTL, sharding) and recommended default profile for hosted vs dedicated modes.

Plan / Test design:
1) Workloads: synth workloads derived from production traces anonymized (see artifact link). Profiles: SHORT-REUSE (20% unique prefixes), MIXED (50% unique), LONG-TAIL (80% unique with some very long prefixes).
2) Variables: cache size (small/medium/large), TTL/eviction policy, prefix-key hashing/sharding, kv-entry memory accounting (approx per-entry bytes).
3) Measurements: hit rate percent, p50/p95/p99 latency of generation, tokens/sec, memory RSS and heap alloc in runtime process, eviction rate, GC pause metrics. Collect per-request KV hit/miss metadata.
4) Harness components: request generator with configurable sequence-length distribution, collector that emits OpenTelemetry metrics to Grafana, and post-run analyzer that computes regressions vs baseline and produces CSV/JSON artifacts.

Artifacts and links:
- Synthetic workload generator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-scripts/tree/kv-harness (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-scripts/pull/142)
- Baseline artifacts (golden): https://drive.redwood.ai/kv-benchmarks/golden-2026-02-15
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-cache/kv-cache-hitrate-latency
- Analysis notebook (Colab/Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/kv-bench-analysis-2026-03-10.ipynb

Preliminary findings (first run 2026-03-05):
- SHORT-REUSE: with cache size 128MB hit rate 78% -> p95 45ms, tokens/sec 520; memory RSS +22MB vs baseline process.
- MIXED: hit rate 54% -> p95 110ms, tokens/sec 210; observed periodic GC spikes causing p95 outliers when eviction bursts occur.
- LONG-TAIL: hit rate 18% -> p95 250ms, tokens/sec 95; memory overhead dominated by large sparse prefix entries.
- Notable: Similar hit rates across runs produced different p95 when eviction patterns differed (burst evictions cause lock contention).

Open issues found:
- KV eviction path uses a global lock in the current runtime; causes p95 tail spikes under bursty evictions (ENG-9200 workstream).
- Memory accounting underestimates per-entry overhead for composite prefix keys leading to optimistic sizing.
- Telemetry stamp missing correlation id for per-request KV access spans (makes root-cause of tail latency harder).

Action items / next experiments:
- Short term (this sprint): add per-shard eviction counters and replace global eviction lock with per-shard mutex (spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/588). Owner: Marco Ruiz.
- Mid term: add approximate memory estimator preflight to avoid overcommitting cache in configuration. Owner: Priya Nair.
- CI gating: add nightly regression job that runs MIXED profile for 2 hours, stores artifact and fails if thresholds crossed. Owner: SRE (oncall rotation).

Acceptance / Rollout criteria:
- Merge harness into benchmark-scripts repo with tests and documentation.
- Nightly job Green for 7 consecutive runs before enabling regression block on pull requests that modify cache code.
- Provide a short runbook for oncall to interpret alerts (links to dashboard and artifact locations).

Notes on trade-offs and decisions:
- We intentionally choose end-to-end tokens/sec and p95 as primary gates instead of raw hit rate because hit rate alone hides concurrency effects and eviction bursts.
- Memory vs latency curve is non-linear: small cache increases near working set boundary produce large hit-rate gains but also risk eviction churn; we will recommend conservative default cache reservation and autoscaling rules for Dedicated pools.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Engineering (runtime): Marco Ruiz (assignee), Priya Nair, Leo Zhang.
- SRE: Daniela Gomez (nightly job), Tobias Müller (alerting).
- PM: Rowan Lee (product owner).

Next update: 2026-03-15 with results from per-shard eviction change and updated nightly job config.
